---
title: "Your coding buddy"
---

Last year you asked an AI tutor questions and typed every line of code
yourself. This year you get a second kind of helper: a **coding agent**, a
program that reads your project, writes into your files, and runs commands in
your terminal. The agent is called `pi`, and the model behind it is hosted by
your school's Novedu platform. This chapter connects the two. You do it once,
and it works for the whole year.

## What the coding buddy is, and is not {#sec-buddy-what}

The model behind `pi` has been given the rules of this course. It knows the
starter project, the coding style your teachers expect, and, most important,
which part of the book you are in. A coding agent in the wild would happily
answer a question about a button with a class, a generic, and three arrow
functions. Yours stays at your level: if your code has no classes yet, it
writes none. When you ask for something the book hasn't covered, it tells you
so and then does it anyway, because you asked.

Two things never change:

* Every line the agent writes is a line you must be able to explain. Exams
  happen without the agent, and "the AI wrote it" is not an answer.
* The agent's mistakes are your mistakes. Read what it changed before you
  commit it.

## Install pi {#sec-buddy-install}

`pi` is a command-line program. Open a terminal and run the installer from
[pi.dev](https://pi.dev):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows, run that line in Git Bash or in WSL. Close the terminal, open a
new one, and check that `pi --version` prints a version number.

## Tell pi where the model is {#sec-buddy-models}

`pi` keeps its settings in a folder named `.pi/agent` inside your home folder.
Two files in that folder matter here. The first, `models.json`, says where the
Novedu endpoint is and what the model is called. It is the same for everybody
in the course, so copy it as it is:

```json
{{< include ../models.json >}}
```

Save it as `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (on Windows:
`C:\Users\<you>\.pi\agent\models.json`). Create the folder if it is missing.

## Add your key {#sec-buddy-key}

The second file, `auth.json`, holds the **activity code**. Your teacher hands
it out in class. The code is the key that opens the door to the model, so it
is not printed in this book. Create `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` with this content
and put the code in place of the placeholder:

```json
{
  "novedu": {
    "type": "api_key",
    "key": "<activity code from your teacher>"
  }
}
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## The key is for your class

Treat the code like a password. Do not post it anywhere, and do not commit
`auth.json` into a git repository. It can expire; if `pi` reports an
authentication error, ask your teacher for a new one.
:::

## First run {#sec-buddy-first-run}

Open a terminal in your to-do list project from the previous chapters and
start the agent:

```bash
pi
```

In the `pi` prompt, pick the model with `/model` and choose *Coding buddy for
the Creative Coding 2 course*. Then type a first task:

> Add a button "Clear done" below the list that removes every item marked as
> done.

Watch what happens. The agent reads `index.html` and `src/index.ts`, proposes
a change, and applies it. Run `npm start`, add a few items, mark two as done,
and click the new button. Then open `src/index.ts` and read the new lines.
Could you have written them? Could you explain them to the person next to
you? If not, ask the agent to walk you through them. That conversation is the
real exercise of this chapter.

## Exercise: take it back {#sec-buddy-exercise}

The agent's code is only useful if it could have been yours. Prove it:

1. Read what `pi` changed. The agent lists the files it touched; open each
   one and compare it with what you remember writing. If you made a copy of
   the project before starting, compare the two folders.
2. Write down, in one sentence each, what every new line does. A line you
   cannot explain is a question for the agent: "Explain line 12 to me, I don't
   understand why it loops backwards."
3. Delete the agent's change and write the button yourself, without `pi`.
   Use what you already have: `querySelectorAll` is not in your toolbox yet,
   so loop over `list.children` and collect the items whose `classList`
   contains `done` before you remove them.
4. Compare your version with the agent's. Different is fine. Wrong is not,
   so test both the same way.

::: {.callout-tip}
## When the agent is the wrong tool

The agent is for getting unstuck and for work you already understand. Before an
exam, practice without it. A good test: close `pi`, delete what it wrote, and
write it again yourself.
:::
